summary: Iter36 regression of Ibn Khaldun (falsafa/inclassables) R2 sync — all 3 previously-failing behaviors now pass. 9/9 backend tests green. Course r2_prefix correct, both episodes stream real audio bytes (206 Partial Content, audio/mp4) from R2 via proxy, and biblio label is dynamically extracted from DOCX. Al-Kindi biblio regression check also passes.

minor.issue: r2_audio_key is None on both Ibn Khaldun episodes even though review request expected it populated (file_key and r2_key are correctly set). Streaming works because /stream and /stream-url read file_key. Migration v15l sets file_key + r2_key but not r2_audio_key. Cosmetic/consistency only — no functional impact.

action_items: (Optional/minor) In migration v15l also set r2_audio_key alongside file_key/r2_key for schema consistency across the 3 parallel field names.
critical_code_review_comments: Three parallel field names on audios (file_key, r2_audio_key, r2_key) — this iteration proved the ambiguity by leaving r2_audio_key None; consolidate to one canonical field with the other two as computed aliases.
Migration v15l is idempotent-ish but relies on hardcoded audio ids — if seed ids change again it will silently no-op.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_iter35_ibn_khaldun_r2.py now has 9 tests including real byte-range streaming (206) and Al-Kindi biblio regression. Audio ids use '-main-' segment (aud_cours-falsafa-inclassables-main-ep01/02). All 3 fixes from iter35 confirmed working end-to-end.
rca of the issue: Fixed. v15l now writes file_key + r2_key + is_placeholder=false so stream endpoints (which read file_key) can serve audio; DOCX title extraction is now applied to DB-registered biblios in list_course_resources so the label is dynamic. Verified via HTTP 206 partial-content responses with audio/mp4 content-type on both episodes and via non-generic biblio label.
